items.label: CoreWeave press release: CoreWeave Delivers NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Performance at (09-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CoreWeave announced the availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 on CoreWeave, with Cognition

set.signal: CoreWeave announced the availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 on CoreWeave, with Cognition (the applied AI lab behind Devin) as what CoreWeave calls the first customer anywhere running production workloads on the system; Cognition worked with CoreWeave to stand up a Vera Rubin NVL72 cluster in early September. Customers run the system under the same operating model and tooling as their existing NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 fleets. In Cognition's own benchmarks on CoreWeave Cloud, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered a 4.8 times increase in total token throughput for its SWE-2 inference workloads versus a GB200 NVL72 baseline and a 3.8 times boost in output token throughput for reinforcement learning workloads. CoreWeave says it has published measured silicon performance on the platform showing 10 times the token throughput per megawatt over NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 on the DeepSeek R1 reasoning model at matched interactivity. Per the release, Cognition, which runs training, reinforcement learning and production inference for Devin on CoreWeave, scaled from bridge capacity to thousands of GPUs for training and inference in less than nine months. EVP Chen Goldberg: having a customer 'already seeing performance gains within days' is the payoff from years of engineering across GPU generations. The release adds that NVIDIA Volta GPUs (relationship with NVIDIA dating to 2017) are still in commercial service on CoreWeave Cloud.

items.reason: The release does not say the nine-month scale-up to thousands of GPUs happened on CoreWeave; it states Cognition runs its workloads on CoreWeave and, separately, that the company scaled in under nine months. Reworded to what the release states.
items.evidence: Cognition, the applied AI lab behind Devin, runs training, reinforcement learning and production inference for Devin on CoreWeave. The company scaled from bridge capacity to thousands of GPUs for training and inference in less than nine months.

items.label: HPE press release: HPE secures its first AMD Helios order in $1.2 billion deal (09-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: HPE announced a $1.2 billion order from Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI Rack by HPE systems

set.signal: HPE announced a $1.2 billion order from Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI Rack by HPE systems at Vultr's cloud data center locations in the United States - HPE's first order for the new AMD Helios system, which features purpose-built HPE Networking scale-up switching and software. Each Helios rack integrates 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs with AMD EPYC 'Venice' CPUs, AMD Pensando Vulcano AI NICs and ROCm software; HPE Networking purpose-built for Helios includes six HPE Juniper Networking QFX5252 scale-up Ethernet switch trays per rack connecting all 72 GPUs, and the release says HPE Services brings expertise in end-to-end deployment and liquid cooling for large AI clusters. The order builds on nearly three years of collaboration between Vultr and Juniper Networks. CEO Antonio Neri: 'AI is driving the largest infrastructure buildout in history'; Helios by HPE 'demonstrates HPE's unique ability to engineer the complete AI architecture with rack-scale compute, scale-up networking, and direct liquid cooling'.

items.reason: The release describes HPE Services' expertise in end-to-end deployment and liquid cooling generically; it does not state that HPE Services covers deployment and liquid cooling under this order. Reworded to the release's own statement.
items.evidence: HPE Services reduces project and operational risk through expertise in end-to-end deployment and liquid-cooling for large AI clusters.
